Alex — thanks for the numbers, that’s very helpful. I sketched an initial shortlist and sizing assumptions based on the profile you shared. Attached is a lightweight template if you want to drop sample prompts.

High-level shortlist (initial candidates):
1) Mistral-7B-v0 (fp16) — strong balance of latency/cost, good for instruction-style prompts
2) BloomX-13B-q4_0 — higher accuracy for multi-document synthesis, higher memory but good for bursty loads
3) Redbird-3B-quant (q4f16) — lowest cost option for high-volume simple completions (lower hallucination risk for short templates)

Context length guidance:
- 4k default for standard synthesis workflows (covers most example chains)
- 8k for multi-doc summarization / long-context workflows (opt-in)
- 16k only for experimental features — significant cost and latency hit

Initial token math (back-of-envelope):
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + response): 210
- Requests/day: 125k -> ~26.25M tokens/day -> ~787.5M tokens/month
- With 30% growth headroom and accounting for system prompts/caching, use planning band: 1.0B — 1.2B tokens/month

Operational notes / asks:
- If you can share 48–72 hours of actual request logs (anonymized) we can tighten the estimate and recommend quantization profiles.
- Would prefer to start with Mistral-7B as a canary, keep BloomX as an accuracy fallback, and use Redbird for bulk cheap inference where results are short/templated.

I’ve cc’d Lauren from CS for the implementation timeline and Monica from solutions to validate the token math.

Regards,
Diego Fernández

Subject: Re: Peregrine — initial token estimates (fwd)

Team — reviewed Monica’s sheet. A few recommendations from infra/opt: 
1) Canary: start with 2x Mistral-7B (fp16) nodes behind the route, autoscale to 6 nodes for steady-state concurrency if using 4k context. This gives headroom for 180 concurrent requests.
2) Quantization: run q4f16 for BloomX-13B to cut cost ~35% while preserving accuracy. Mistral runs fine in fp16; we can test a q4 variant for extra throughput.
3) Caching: implement prefix/KV caching for document chunks (expected to reduce token load by ~12–18% for repeat doc access).
4) Routing policy: default to Mistral for user-facing flows, fallback to BloomX for multi-doc synth with high-length heuristics, redirect short templated responses to Redbird.

Bandwidth/latency notes: expect 1.5–2x token-latency for 8k vs 4k contexts; call this out to product.

I also added a quick rollout plan in the HubSpot deal (see link). Recommend a 4-week pilot with weekly checkpoints and a canary traffic ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Vivek
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
